source: LIVE GET https://algovault.com/api/merkle-batches (cache-busted). HTTP 200, 37771 B, application/json; charset=utf-8, NO cache-control header on the response.
change_class: NO KEY CHANGE — the top-level key set is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the 2026-07-21 snapshot allowed_keys (7). What this snapshot ADDS is a forbidden_values contract.
change_note: The on-chain anchor surface. Its no-data-loss invariant was already canaried by the on-chain/dashboard equality check, but its VALUES were gated by nobody. Measured at capture: totalCalls 646373 on /api/performance-public >= total_signals 644116 here, so that equality canary holds.
supersedes: audits/api-merkle-batches-shape-snapshot-2026-07-21.json — superseded, not edited away. That file is KEPT ON DISK and gains exactly TWO appended keys (superseded_by + superseded_reason) and nothing else; the per-file jq semantic-equality proof runs in this wave's CH3 gate. The append is REQUIRED, not cosmetic: build-knowledge-json.mjs projects every audits/*-shape-snapshot-*.json into the PUBLIC knowledge bundle and knowledge-index.ts keys each document response_shape:<endpoint>, so two LIVE files carrying /api/merkle-batches are a duplicate document id, which winkBM25S rejects outright: KnowledgeIndex.build() THROWS (Error: winkBM25S: Duplicate document encountered: response_shape:<endpoint>), tests/integration/knowledge-flow.test.ts fails, and at runtime the lazily-constructed index behind search_knowledge / chat_knowledge cannot be built. MEASURED CORRECTION, kept visible because the instrument matters: `npm run build:knowledge` TOLERATES the duplicate and exits 0 reporting response_shapes=39, so the builder succeeding is NOT evidence the bundle is usable — the rejection lives in the INDEX, not the build. A non-empty superseded_by is the ONLY thing that excludes a snapshot from that projection.

error_contract.description: Unchanged from 2026-07-21, restated as an OBJECT rather than a string — a FIX, not a reformat: build-knowledge-json.mjs only projects error_contract when typeof === object, so the previous string reached the public knowledge bundle as an empty object.
error_contract.behaviour: HTTP 500 with a Failed-to-load-batches error body on throw. getMerkleBatchSummary() is awaited in the SAME Promise.all as getMerkleBatches(), so a summary failure degrades identically to a batches failure — it cannot half-render.

cache_contract.description: MEASURED 2026-09-10: NO cache-control header on the response. The 2026-07-21 snapshot recorded a Cloudflare edge Cache Rule (45s) as a system-map annotation — an EDGE rule, which does not appear as an origin response header, so the two records do not contradict each other.
cache_contract.staleness_signal: NONE on this body. Publish liveness is watched by its own producer-side canary, per the freshness law: freshness alarms measure PRODUCERS, never rendered artifacts.

consumers: LANDING /verify badge + chip (data-tr-field latest_batch, latest_batch_n, latest_batch_at)
SIGNAL /track-record function-rendered page — inline merkle-stats block + data-tr-field merkle_batch_count (src/index.ts; uses batch_count + total_signals + latest_batch_id)
landing/js/track-record-proxy.js (runtime hydration — latest_batch_id / batch_count, row-derived fallback for mid-deploy skew)
scripts/render-integrations.mjs + scripts/refresh-integrations-numbers.mjs (baked batchCount fallback — use batch_count)
scripts/snapshot-landing-data.mjs (deploy-time injector; accessor batches.latest.batch_id was ALREADY correct, unchanged)

anchors_at_capture.note: returned_rows (100) < batch_count (153) BY DESIGN — batches[] is LIMIT-capped at 100 while batch_count is the scalar COUNT(*). This is the capped-collection trap OPS-CAPPED-COLLECTION-GUARD-W1 exists for: a consumer reading batches.length publishes 100 and diverges +1/day. Every assertion below keys on the SCALAR.

forbidden_values._doc: Assertions are STRUCTURAL (path + predicate) or VALUE-REGEX over the stringified body, never a bare string ban. The positive rows deliberately assert the SCALAR counters and never batches.length — see anchors_at_capture.note.
forbidden_values.enforced_by: scripts/check-served-surface-values.mjs (SERVED_SURFACE_VALUES_VERDICT). live_only — reached by --live, scheduled as ops/cron/served-surface-values-canary.sh on signal-1. The clean/violating proof pair below runs OFFLINE in --self-test, which deploy.yml runs fail-closed.

assertions.reason: CLAUDE.md Data Integrity LAW: outcome WR is INTERNAL ONLY and must never be exposed via MCP/API/landing/README. This surface anchors signal batches on-chain; leaking a realised return here would publish the internal series under a proof banner.

The 2026-07-21 forbidden_keys list, now enforced instead of documented. A batch row commits to a merkle_root and a COUNT; the verdicts inside the batch are the paid product and are only revealed by /api/verify-signal against a hash the caller already holds.

THE OTHER DIRECTION, and it is keyed on the SCALARS on purpose. batches[] is LIMIT-capped at 100; batch_count is COUNT(*) = 153 at capture. Never aggregate over a capped collection — that defect published 100 merkle batches while the real count was 109 and diverging daily.
The proof is worthless without the chain and contract it is anchored to. A verifier that cannot locate the contract cannot verify anything, so these travel with the counts.

proof._doc: R3.4 — a gate never observed catching the defect it was built for is not evidence. Both directions: the CLEAN body must produce ZERO violations, the VIOLATING body must produce some. Without the clean leg the proof is satisfied by a contract that fails on everything. Run by --self-test, therefore by deploy.yml, therefore on every deploy.
violating_mutations: batch_count = null  (the OTHER direction: the scalar counter nulled)

drift_check._doc: NOT a drift_check_command shell string. That form was measured to have never run once. This names an executable script and its verdict token.

modes.offline: NOT APPLICABLE to this surface. It is served from algovault.com and this repo exports no pure builder for it, so coverage is live_only. The clean/violating proof pair IS the offline leg.
modes.live: --live [baseUrl]. Fetches the deployed surface, cache-busted, and asserts these rules. SCHEDULED as ops/cron/served-surface-values-canary.sh, crontab 47 7 * * * on signal-1, alert SERVED_SURFACE_VALUE_DRIFT. A transport failure is INDETERMINATE, never FAIL.

proven_able_to_fail: The clean/violating pair above is executed by scripts/check-served-surface-values.mjs --self-test on every deploy. The mutations were observed producing violations before this file was committed; the clean body was observed producing none.
